records.title: Payroll jobs
records.population: Payroll jobs in motion picture and sound recording industries (NAICS 512)
records.definition: All-employee payroll jobs, not seasonally adjusted. This is a count of jobs, not unique workers.
records.limitation: Includes sound recording and occupations beyond actors. Does not measure freelance livelihoods, individual earnings, or whether a particular worker can find work.

records.title: On-location shoot days
records.geography: Greater Los Angeles jurisdictions served by FilmLA
records.population: Permitted on-location activity reported by FilmLA across all reported categories
records.definition: FilmLA shoot days: permitted filming activity at a location on a day. Multiple locations can contribute multiple shoot days to one production.
records.limitation: Coverage follows FilmLA's permitting jurisdictions. This is not soundstage occupancy, unique productions, employment, or a complete count of filming everywhere in LA.

gaps.title: Actor income and hours
gaps.question: What do people classified as actors earn, and how many hours do they work?
gaps.note: No reviewed actor-income series. Payroll jobs count jobs in motion picture and sound recording industries. They are not earnings, and they are not a count of actors.

gaps.title: Who controls the companies
gaps.question: Which companies share a parent, and how concentrated is the business?
gaps.note: No reviewed ownership or concentration series. Studio revenue on the lot is a quarterly total for a basket of public companies. It does not name a parent or a market share.

gaps.title: Who goes to the movies
gaps.question: Who participates in moviegoing, and what keeps people away?
gaps.note: No reviewed participation survey. Weekend grosses and Netflix hours measure commercial attention for defined lists. They do not measure who attended or whether people liked the work.
